title: The Okeh Artists Ball, February 1926: what she sang
summary: She remembers the big Okeh night, singing "Shorty George" and "Up the Country" with Herschel on piano, and the Wickman Sisters' show.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

blocks.x: Ms. Wallace, I wonder if you'd try to think about that night in 1926, February 27th. That Saturday night that was the O.K. Artists Ball, when the O.K. artists performed that night. Do you remember that night?
Yeah, I really do remember that night.
Yeah, that was the time of my life. I was pretty young, but I understand it now.
I didn't understand it then, but I understand it now.
Well, would you tell me about it? What do you understand about it now that you didn't understand then?
Yes, ma'am. I hear you, okay. Uh-huh.
What do you understand about it now that you didn't then, because that was a very long time ago, 1926.

Well, it was ______. They had -- it's something like a ______, you know, and they had different ones on the program and so they said that I sang just like the record did, said it was no different to the songs I sing --
Do you remember what songs you sang that night?
And that's what I sang, yes.
Who played the piano for you?

Uh-huh. And he said, "______, she sounds just like the record, just like the record." So this -- the people that ______ they invited her, but she was there. See, she wasn't on the program, but they call her anyhow.

Yeah, and she was singing on Columbia Records, but this was supposed to be the O.K. But the Wickman Sisters came that night, so they called them to sing a number and she sang "Sweet Georgia Brown." And I don't know who played "Sweet Georgia Brown" for her now, but I remember (singing). And we just laughed, the way she carried on. She said, "Two left feet, oh so neat is Sweet Georgia Brown."
Somebody stole her bracelet. She had a diamond bracelet and somebody stole it.
